review.cadence: quarterly and before every minor release

statusDefinitions.meaning: Reviewed, shipped, versioned, conformance-tested, and owned.
statusDefinitions.claim: Only the named bounded capabilities and fixtures.

statusDefinitions.meaning: A reviewable preview exists without a stable support promise.
statusDefinitions.claim: Explicit opt-in or contributor-preview use only.

statusDefinitions.meaning: A plausible candidate lacks sufficient demand, evidence, ownership, or capacity for a pilot.
No adapter or safe boundary is provided by the project.
statusDefinitions.claim: The input remains outside the support claim and must not be guessed.

criteria.title: Demand and problem fit
criteria.threshold: Name users, architecture questions, independent demand signals, and the gap the bounded adapter closes.
criteria.requiredEvidence: A public proposal with demand signals and competing-workflow analysis.

criteria.title: Graph and evidence mapping
criteria.threshold: Map the first construct slice to nodes, edges, identity, source spans, evidence, and unknown diagnostics.
criteria.requiredEvidence: A language-neutral mapping and intentional non-equivalence record.

criteria.title: Measurable correctness
criteria.threshold: Target at least 0.90 precision, 0.85 recall, and complete evidence or an explicit unresolved reason.
criteria.requiredEvidence: Positive, negative, ambiguity, conformance, precision, and recall fixtures.

criteria.title: Deterministic bounded execution
criteria.threshold: Repeated canonical output is byte-identical under finite resource and declared toolchain limits.
criteria.requiredEvidence: Repeated local runs, resource budgets, compiler/runtime versions, and fixture provenance.

criteria.title: Authority and isolation
criteria.threshold: Source reads are scoped; network, child processes, dynamic loading, and repository execution are denied.
criteria.requiredEvidence: A manifest, isolation result or documented refusal, and hostile-boundary fixtures.

criteria.title: Maintainers and response
criteria.threshold: A primary owner and backup accept dependency, quality, compatibility, and security responsibility.
criteria.requiredEvidence: Named owner groups, review date, and a security/retirement response path.

criteria.title: Public contract cost
criteria.threshold: Adapter API, compatibility, capability, graph-schema, Node, and compiler dimensions are explicit.
criteria.requiredEvidence: Versioned manifest, matrix row, migration or rejection decision, and schema review.

criteria.title: Sustainable scope
criteria.threshold: The pilot has a bounded construct list, fixture cost, review cadence, and retirement trigger.
criteria.requiredEvidence: A scope note, ownership estimate, and a public transition or retirement record.

entries.name: Sample reference adapter
entries.supportBoundary: Deterministic reference fixtures only; not a production language or framework support claim.
entries.rationale: The reference adapter is the public conformance boundary used to test evidence, identity, unsupported diagnostics, and compatibility negotiation.

entries.name: Bounded Fastify adapter
entries.supportBoundary: Literal Fastify methods, object-form routes, local handlers, and the existing bounded TypeScript graph; dynamic registration remains diagnostic.
entries.rationale: Fastify is the reviewed second TypeScript framework slice; its dynamic and unresolved cases are intentionally retained as diagnostics.

entries.name: Adapter starter example
entries.supportBoundary: Contributor-preview package for learning and review; copying it does not create a stable support promise.
entries.rationale: The starter is intentionally experimental until an independent adapter review graduates a contributor implementation.

entries.name: Rust adapter candidate
entries.supportBoundary: No Rust source analysis or language-level support claim is made; any future pilot must pass the selection and E-005 gates.
entries.rationale: Rust is a plausible language-neutral pilot, but demand, bounded construct scope, and maintenance ownership are intentionally deferred to a future public proposal.

entries.name: Python adapter
entries.supportBoundary: Python repositories are outside the current adapter boundary; no Python graph is inferred or advertised.
entries.rationale: No maintained Python adapter, pilot evidence, or security/ownership review exists, so the project must not imply support from language-neutral types alone.
